It is objectively worse than the original trilogy. It had an absolutely ABYSMAL release but it was slightly tweaked/fixed to make it more enjoyable. I've played through it a couple of times and I kinda got bored nearing the end getting to the [spoiler]Meridian[/spoiler] . It could be because I spent a lot of the time messing with the settlement system. The APEX system doesn't make *much* sense in the context of a game like this and the settlements can take quite a bit of time to fill out. About half of the characters annoy the ♥♥♥♥ out of me, specifically Peebee and Cora. Ryder themselves is nowhere near as charming and likeable as the OG Commander Shepard.

The combat is actually fun, though MUCH different from the original trilogy. The characters I do like are very good,  like Vetra, Jaal, Nakmor and Suvi. Though the settlement stuff takes up quite a bit of time while you are playing, it is cool to have something other than the main story to work on, unlike ME-LE.
I still enjoyed the game overall and will probably play through it again in the future. 

Would I say its worth it full price? No.
However, much like ME-LE it goes on sale very frequently. Get it while it is on sale and you will spend your money much better.

ME:A was always a mixed bag for me. I played the game through twice, once on my xbox, once on steam. There's a lot of things that they got wrong but there's still a bit of things that they got right. I think Andromeda is worth playing at least once even if the experience is nowhere near as good as the trilogy. Andromeda pulls quite bit from ME1 with the exploration, vehicle driving, and some other stuff. The Nomad aint the Mako but it is still fun to drive. Fortunately exploration in Andromeda isn't like in ME1 where they make you scale a mountain at a near 90 degree angle just so you can survey a mineral which was arguably the most annoying thing in ME1. 

Combat really differs from the trilogy, as the trilogy really favored you to use and shoot from cover, Andromeda favors maneuvering and fast pace moving to flank enemies. The combat profiles allow you to pick whatever playstyle you want with no regard to class restrictions so while it gives you a ton of tools to use, it kills replayability. In the trilogy, Shepard was limited to weapons (except ME3) and skills your class had (except for the one extra ability you could choose in ME2 and 3). I hope that the next ME goes back to class restrictions otherwise what's the point of classes?

The writing is definitely subpar to what you would expect from both ME and Bioware, but leagues above DA Veilguard (Veilguard makes me worry about the next ME). Conversations Ryder has no real purpose in the choices because instead of renegade and paragon choices, it gives you casual, professional, emotional, and logical choices. These don't do anything except change your reply slightly. Conversation options also tend to be misleading for what Ryder will actually say. For big choices, once again doesn't matter as your decisions will slightly alter conversations and since Andromeda obviously  is not getting a sequel, none of the choices will carry into the next game. Story is pretty mid for ME and the subpar writing doesn't help.

Graphics are good. I do like the art direction of Andromeda quite a bit. The worst part are the character models. They look so robotic, it's painful. 

I didn't touch multiplayer as I don't care for multiplayer for a ME game.

Every year or two end up doing another run of the trilogy but I had to force myself to do a 2nd run of Andromeda. Take that as you will.


TLDR : I recommend playing once, the exploration is fun, the story and writing are subpar, graphics and art are good, character models look awful.
I loved the game. one of the best I have played

It has taken me a long time to convince myself to pick the game back up after getting though the first half of the game back when it came out. 

I was fresh off replaying the original trilogy again, and did not give Andromeda a fair chance, assuming it was going to capture that lighting in a bottle. 

With that said, Andromeda was still a really good game. The pacing could be a bit better in the first half, and some of the characters could have been fleshed out more, but I feel that a second instillation in Andromeda could give us that, much like Mass Effect 2 developing our beloved characters in from Mass Effect 1. I really enjoyed the loyalty missions and the family missions to unlock you fathers memories. It just felt that you had to slog to get to the juicy bits of the game. It was worth it, but I really felt like I had to work for it.

I know Mass Effect Andromeda was considered a failure after release (more or less) and the next Mass Effect is a departure from Andromeda, but I now realize that it is a real shame. The writers really nailed the last half of the game in terms of writing and pacing, and I think a sequel could have really taken off from the revelations in the last half of the game. 

You can play this without playing the original trilogy, but the game does make some references to the original trilogy. Not in a way that makes the game unplayable. With that said, it would be interesting to hear someone's perspective if they played Andromeda first then the original trilogy. 

All that is to say, I would suggest playing even just once. And Vetra is best girl and I would romance her again.
